title: Seed banks
titleCn: 种子银行：从古代储藏到现代基因保险

paragraphs.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Hello. Today, there are nearly two thousand seed banks in the world. Seed banks are places where seeds from millions of different plants are stored to keep them safe for the future. Today, I'd like to tell you a little bit about seed banks and how and why they're used.
So let's look at some history, and we'll start in ancient Mesopotamia around eight thousand BC.
This was when the ancient Mesopotamians started to practice agriculture. They were the first to do so as far as we know.

Every year, they would harvest their crops for food, but they also used some of these crops to make clothing. As well as this, they also collected the seeds, so they would have crops for the following year or years.
Thanks to archaeologists, we now know how these seeds were stored.
When examining ancient settlements in Mesopotamia, archaeologists found the precious seeds underground, stored in baskets.
After much examination, they concluded that in order to protect the seeds, they were combined with large quantities of ash from old fires before being buried.
Archaeologists wanted to establish why seeds were buried underground and concluded the most likely threat was posed by animals who might have found them a good food source.
Today, there are many more reasons why we need to protect seeds, and that's why we have sophisticated facilities like seed banks.
Seed banks provide a type of insurance against the very damaging effects that climate change is bringing to the natural world.
Extreme weather events like floods can wipe out entire crops.
Seed banks are also necessary because they can help to reduce the crop losses that can result if a disease occurs in a certain type of plant.

Importantly too, seed banks allow scientists to discover how different plants can be used in the production of medicine. Many plants have healing properties that we are only just now beginning to understand, and having banks of seeds means that we will hopefully always have them around to study and use.

Scientists need to be able to identify the plants and maintain accurate records. For this reason, each sample collected is then assigned a special code, which scientists around the world can recognize.

The seeds need, of course, to be cleaned. There are many different ways of doing this. Whichever technique is used, this process occurs in an environmentally controlled room in which the temperature is kept constant. Furthermore, the humidity is strictly monitored to make sure it doesn't change too much. All of this helps to ensure the quality of the specimen.

The seeds need then to be stored in a safe environment. To do this, scientists freeze the seeds at very low temperatures, about minus twenty degrees Celsius. Then the scientists place these frozen seeds in specially designed airtight canisters, and they do this in order to protect the seeds from contamination, something we really don't want.

One thing that might surprise you about seed banks is that they don't just contain edible plants. Scientists also include plants that are known to be poisonous and which can cause sickness, as these plants might one day be useful.
Although governments have financed the setting up of some of these seed banks, they're expensive to run, and many require ongoing donations from the public to help support them.
Okay, let me now tell you-
That is the end of part four. You now have one minute to check your answers to part four.
